chunks: O you who believe, do not be like those who deny, and say of their brethren (who died) travelling in the land or fighting: 'Had they stayed with us here they would not have died or been killed.' This happened so that God may fill their hearts with grief. God is the giver of life and death and sees all that you do.

key_terms.ضَرَبُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ: traveled or moved through the land
key_terms.يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ: He gives life and causes death

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'Had they stayed with us, they would not have died' in Surah Aal-Imran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse critiques the pre-Islamic notion of 'absence as cause' (ghayb) by affirming that death and martyrdom are direct manifestations of Divine Will (Mashi'ah) and Knowledge (Ilm). It serves as a theological foundation for understanding that while human effort is necessary, the ultimate outcome—whether life or death—is determined by Allah, thereby transforming the believer's perspective on sacrifice in battle from mere chance to divine decree.
